correctness.rationale: The top-two connectivity characterization is exact because any induced bipartite subgraph with representatives from both shores is connected. Earliest opposite-shore candidate at position L+1 requires at least L-1 adjacent swaps to reach position 2; moving it directly achieves the bound. Without-replacement falling-factorial counts yield P(X>=d)=((a)_{d+1}+(b)_{d+1})/(m)_{d+1}; the given mass and mean formulas follow. Mean simplifies to (m²-3ab-1)/(ab+m+1), monotone in ab, giving star/balanced extrema and known star specialization. Asymptotic limits follow respectively from uniform order statistics, logarithms of survival products, and finite-position color convergence. Independent exhaustive shortest-path BFS on all permutations through m=7 checks finite cases. The stated result is only for complete bipartite graphs and uniform rankings.

evidence: General-graph nearest-domain optimization is NP-hard in the structured-domains paper, which does not yield complete bipartite closed form. The Condorcet paper concerns (weak) Condorcet graph domains, while K_{a,b} for a,b>=2 has cycles and is not generally a Condorcet domain.
